judged_text: The rewritten public `GroupsController#members` feeds the user-supplied `limit` straight into `group.users.limit(limit)` with no server-side upper bound (`limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i`). Any visitor who can see a group sends `?limit=100000000` and receives the group's entire membership serialized in one response — for the visible automatic `everyone` group that is the site's full user list — so the pagination this diff adds is trivially bypassed and each such request is a cheap heavy DB/serialization load for the site operator.

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupsController#members`, the new pagination logic sets `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and then directly applies it via `group.users.order(:username_lower).limit(limit).offset(offset)` with no server-side maximum. This makes it trivially possible for any requester who can access the endpoint to pass an arbitrarily large `limit` and force heavy DB/serialization work (and effectively bypass pagination).
